input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: After stripping ANSI codes the prompt text is also passed through str.strip(), which removes the whitespace at the end of the prompt that separates it from the user's typed input.
- failure path: click.prompt("Name") builds the prompt 'Name: '; when the stream does not support color (piped output, CliRunner, NO_COLOR) the prompt is shown as 'Name:' with the cursor glued to the colon, while on a color-capable terminal the same call keeps the trailing space, so transcripts differ between the two environments.

Reviewer finding
- description: When ANSI is stripped, the prompt text is also stripped of leading and trailing whitespace, which the commit title does not mention. A prompt such as "Name: " is shown as "Name:" with no trailing space.
- rationale: Trigger: a prompt whose text ends in a space (the usual form, e.g. prompt("Name: ")) is run on a stream that does not support ANSI, such as a redirected or piped stderr/stdout. Mechanism: strip_ansi(text).strip() removes the trailing space along with the codes. Impact: the user sees the prompt run into the typed input ("Name:John"), and the output differs from the same prompt on a color-capable terminal, even though the change should only remove escape codes.
critique: The finding names the same mechanism: calling .strip() after strip_ansi removes the trailing space when the stream does not support color. It also gives the same result, the prompt running into the user's input and output that differs from a color-capable terminal.
